#6243. Nomad Citizen: A New Social Safety Net for Entrepreneurs

If you’re a digital nomad or a location-independent business owner, you’re either overpaying for fragmented insurance coverage (travel, medical, etc.) or just badly underinsured. You have a health plan, travel insurance, and maybe some medical evacuation coverage. But, when you work for yourself, you lack the kind of safety net protections you get with a corporate job. And you cannot use a country’s social safety net because, well, you’re not a citizen, right? You’re just roaming the world!

The travel insurance company Safety Wing is looking to change that. They have always wanted to create this all-in-one package for digital nomads that includes insurance, employee benefits, and a social safety net.

I use their travel insurance all the time and they have just launched what they call Nomad Citizen that seeks to address the gaps in coverage.

Nomad Citizen is an annual membership that bundles health coverage, travel protection, income protection, and life insurance benefits into a single plan. It’s for location-independent entrepreneurs and business owners who spend more than half the year outside their home country and whose lives and income cross borders as a default.

Nomad Citizen covers you globally with no residency restrictions (except for Puerto Rico).

Nomad Citizen covers people under 56 and earning at least $4,000 USD per month. You sign up online, choose your start date, declare that you’re in good health, and confirm you’ll be outside your passport country for more than half the year. You can also add your partner and any children under 18.

But who should sign-up? This is an interesting product. I definitely think there’s a niche for it. After all, let’s say you’re an entrepreneur in Bali and don’t have access to any social safety net. What happens if you get sick or really hurt and you’re out of work? A friend of mine in Mexico was hit by a car and severely hospitalized and ate into his travel insurance limits really quickly. Afterwards, he couldn’t work for months while he was in rehab and started a GoFundMe for help. A product like Nomadic Citizen would have helped him. Or helped any of the other digital nomads who get injured on the road and have to raise funds.

I think this product is good for someone who is living in a country outside their own without access to social services and a robust social safety net. For example, if you live in Sweden and have access to all the benefits of the State, this product probably isn’t for you because they have tons of services but if you live in Thailand, Mexico, Indonesia, or France but don’t have access to benefits, or are just roaming the world, have a high income, work on your own, or have a family, then this product would be something to consider.

For those signing up on or after July 1, 2026, the Nomad Citizen membership costs $443 per month for those 18 to 39. If you’re 40 – 49, it’s $665 per month, and $875 per month for 50-55. Children cost $143 per month (couples on the plan can add their first child under 10 at no cost). You can pay monthly or annually.

A note about US coverage: Nomad Citizen is truly worldwide, including the US, although it should be noted that coverage limits were not designed for extensive use there…because well, the US health care system is just a mess.

Income protection: The income protection benefit is probably the single most compelling reason Nomad Citizen exists. Traditional income protection or disability insurance requires a fixed employer, a permanent address, and residency in a specific country. Freelancers and sole traders working across borders are essentially uninsurable for income loss through conventional schemes, such as government assistance.

If you’re a freelancer or remote worker and you lose your income (you’re laid off, your contracts dry up, or you can’t work due to a medical condition), Nomad Citizen pays you up to $4,000 per month for up to 3 or 6 months while you get back on your feet. That benefit doesn’t exist anywhere else!

Health insurance: Up to $1.5 million in annual coverage for inpatient, outpatient, prescriptions, dental, vision, mental health, maternity, preventive care, wellness therapies, and more. This is just like health insurance where you live and covers everything you need. It is far more robust than regular travel insurance, which is only there for emergencies.

Travel coverage: Trip delays, cancellations, stolen electronics, lost luggage, evacuation, robbery, family visits during hospitalisation.

Parental leave: If you have a baby or become a legal guardian of a child, they pay US$4,000/month so you can take time off work without worrying about money. There is a waiting period of 3 years to access this benefit.

Long-term disability: If something really serious happens to you and you are permanently forced to stop working because, for instance,  you lose your eyesight, you’re diagnosed with cancer, you have a major stroke, or you can no longer do basic things like walk, dress yourself, or eat on your own, they pay you US$4,000/month up to age 75.

Visa assistance: Members can browse and apply for different governments’ versions of long-term visas designed for nomads (i.e. they can work on those visas) directly through our app interface without having to apply through the government websites. They handle all the direct communication with the government and quality check your application before submission to maximize the chances of approval.

Nomad Care Map: Find the best providers through their member-powered database of more than 4000 healthcare providers all over the world, with ratings for service and English level.

Payment cards: Use your SafetyWing card to pay for covered services up to $500. This auto-generates a claim that has already been paid so you do not have to wait for reimbursement. The SafetyWing card is a worldwide prepaid debit card that is sent to every Nomad Citizen member, which they can use to pay for doctor’s appointments or prescriptions without using their own money.

24/7 human support: You’ll have access to 24/7 live chat so you can get an answer from a real person within a few minutes.

Everything in one app: Claims, coverage details, customer care, provider search with Nomad Care Map, and visa assistance are all managed through a single app. There is no need to switch between a health insurer, a travel insurer, and a separate income protection provider (if one existed).

For health coverage, you either pay out of pocket and file for reimbursement or contact the 24/7 team to arrange direct payment with the provider. For travel claims, you collect documentation (police reports, carrier delay notices, receipts) and submit a claim. For income protection, you work with SafetyWing to verify the loss and provide evidence that you’re actively seeking new income. Everything is managed through one app and they make it really simple and easy to do.

I love SafetyWing’s mission and use their travel insurance on all my trips. This new Nomad Citizen product is perfect for people who are full-time digital nomads and want some sort of income protection as well as more robust health and travel coverage and the kind of social safety programs you would get if you lived in one place. After all, when you are a solopreneur, you do worry about what happens if you get injured, can’t work, or have a kid. It’s all on you, right? Nomad Citizen is the program that ensures that you won’t have to worry about this kind of stuff anymore.

#6242. Craving an Island Escape? These Bahamas Airbnbs Are Just What the Doctor Ordered

Growing up in Fort Lauderdale, the Bahamas always felt like an extension of South Florida to me. Just a short flight or boat ride away, the archipelago was somewhere I returned to often, and still do. Yet what continues to surprise me is how different one island can feel from the next. I've always thought it was a shame that so many visitors to the Bahamas never make it beyond Nassau or Freeport. Eleuthera has some of the prettiest beaches I've seen, the water around the Exumas is almost unbelievably clear, and the Abacos have small waterfront towns that are worth exploring. Each island has its own personality, and even after years of visiting, there are so many I still want to discover.

Renting a home is one of my favorite ways to experience it all. Beautiful beachfront villas, colorful cottages, and contemporary homes with pools overlooking the sea are everywhere in the Bahamas. Having your own place makes it easy to settle in, explore a little, and enjoy the particular rhythm of whichever island you've chosen. After so many visits, I’m eager to step slightly off the typical tourist path (although the resorts and hotels here are also beautiful), and these Bahamas Airbnbs are a great way to do so. Read on for my most-recommended rentals in the Bahamas, from beachfront stays to island cottages.

We've selected these listings based on Superhost and Guest Favorite status, ratings, amenities, location, decor, editor stays, and previous guest reviews.

Number of guests: 12 (up to 8 adults and 4 children)Bed and bath: 4 bedrooms, 4.5 bathsWhy we love it: Heated pool, direct beach access, bohemian interiors

With its natural textures, airy interiors, and covered outdoor lounge, Corsair Key feels specially designed for long, unhurried days by the water. Four king bedrooms offer plenty of room for families or friends, while a heated swimming pool and direct beach access make it tempting to stay put. The well-equipped kitchen and generous dining spaces are especially appealing for groups who enjoy cooking together. And with a location in Bimini (the westernmost district of The Bahamas) being so close to South Florida, getting here is surprisingly easy.

Location: Rockwell Island, BiminiThings to do nearby: Radio Beach, Bimini snorkeling, fishing excursions

Check Availability at Homes and Villas by Marriott

Number of guests: 12Bed and bath: 5 bedrooms, 5.5 bathsWhy we love it: Retro design, heated pool, outdoor grill that looks like a vintage VW bus

A vintage Volkswagen bus turned barbecue station isn't something you expect to find at a luxury vacation rental, but that's part of the fun at this quirky, vibrant spot. This five-bedroom bungalow embraces its retro personality with bold artwork, wicker lighting, and colorful bedrooms. Outside, a heated pool is surrounded by tropical landscaping, while Harbour Island's famous pink sands are just a short walk away. It's a playful alternative to more traditional island cottages, with enough room for the whole family; kids will particularly love the bunk beds.

Location: Dunmore Town, Harbour IslandThings to do nearby: Pink Sand Beach, Dunmore Town, Briland's Blue Hole

Number of guests: 7Bed and bath: 3 bedrooms, 2 bathsWhy we love it: Direct beachfront access, waterfront deck, panoramic views

The best feature of this three-bedroom cottage? The uninterrupted sea views, visible through expansive windows and from the waterfront deck. The interiors are simple and contemporary, with an open living space that keeps the focus firmly on the scenery. Spend the morning swimming, take a drive to Tropic of Cancer Beach, or settle in with a book and watch the water change color throughout the afternoon. With three bedrooms—a king, a queen, and a room with a queen and a lofted twin—the property sleeps up to seven.

Location: Moore Hill, Little ExumaThings to do nearby: Tropic of Cancer Beach, Santana's Grill Pit, Little Exuma beaches

Number of guests: 8Bed and bath: 4 bedrooms, 4.5 bathsWhy we love it: Infinity pool, private cinema, ocean views

Location: Aqualina, NassauThings to do nearby: Cable Beach, Baha Mar, Nassau boat excursions

Check Availability at Marriott Home and Villas

Number of guests: 10Bed and bath: 4 bedrooms, 4.5 bathsWhy we love it: Private pool, beachfront setting, covered oceanfront terrace

Vaulted wood ceilings and enormous windows bring warmth and light to this four-bedroom home on Tar Bay, but the outdoor spaces are what make Aquamarine Villa particularly appealing. A private swimming pool overlooks the beach, while a shaded terrace offers a welcome escape from the afternoon sun. The open-plan living area makes gathering easy, and the bedroom configuration—two kings with oceanfront views, a queen, and a room with a queen and a bunk bed—works well for families traveling together. With the sand just steps past the pool, shoes are likely to remain optional for most of the stay.

Location: Tar Bay, Great ExumaThings to do nearby: Hoopers Bay, George Town, Exuma boat excursions

Number of guests: 2Bed and bath: 1 bedroom, 1 bathWhy we love it: Pink-sand beach, heated pool, covered veranda

Neighborhood: Governor's Harbour area, EleutheraThings to do nearby: Pink-sand beaches, Governor's Harbour, local snorkeling

Number of guests: 2Bed and bath: 1 bedroom, 1 bathWhy we love it: Private waterfront deck, bedroom ocean views, optional private chef

Some of the best places to stay in the Bahamas are the ones that make you feel completely surrounded by water. At this intimate one-bedroom retreat on Exuma, enormous bedroom windows look directly toward the sea, and a private deck provides access to the water below. The interiors are understated, with a kitchenette designed for light meals rather than elaborate cooking. A private chef can be arranged for dinner for an added fee, or guests can venture into nearby George Town for a delicious meal at one of the waterfront restaurants.

Location: Near George Town, ExumaThings to do nearby: George Town waterfront, snorkeling, Exuma boat excursions

Number of guests: 14Bed and bath: 5 bedrooms, 4 bathsWhy we love it: Private pool, beachfront location, kayaks and paddleboards

Sea turtles frequently visit the shallow waters of Hoopers Bay, and guests at Blu Wakes have an excellent vantage point for spotting them. The five-bedroom villa—four kings and a room for kids with two queens and a bunk bed—opens onto a beautiful stretch of beach, with a private pool overlooking the water. Kayaks and paddleboards make it easy to explore the bay, while concierge services can arrange everything from a private chef to a day trip exploring the Exuma cays. With room for 14, it's particularly well suited to extended families or big groups.

Location: Hoopers Bay, Great ExumaThings to do nearby: Hoopers Bay sea turtles, George Town, Exuma cays excursions

Number of guests: 2Bed and bath: Studio, 1 bathWhy we love it: Beachfront location, porch, on-site beach bar

There's a clear appeal to a place like this where the biggest morning decision is whether to take your coffee on the porch or at the beach. This cheerful little cottage, called Tiny's Toes in the Sand, has rocking chairs overlooking Salt Pond Harbour, a kitchenette for simple meals, and a beach bar just steps away. At only 400 square feet, it's not a place for spreading out, but for two people looking to spend most of their time steps from the water, that's rather the point.

Location: Salt Pond, Long IslandThings to do nearby: Salt Pond Harbour, Dean's Blue Hole, Cape Santa Maria Beach

Number of guests: 16Bed and bath: 7 bedrooms, 9 bathsWhy we love it: Infinity pool, outdoor kitchen, concierge services

With seven bedrooms and more than 5,000 square feet of living space, Sea Salt Villa is designed for a crowd. The contemporary home sits within a gated community overlooking Emerald Bay, with expansive windows, an infinity pool, and a covered outdoor entertaining area. An outdoor kitchen makes casual dinners easy, while concierge services can help arrange private chefs and excursions. It's a particularly good option for extended families or groups of friends who want the space of a private home but still enjoy resort-style comforts. Plus, it’s located on a PGA golf course if you’re looking to get in a round or two, and guests can rent golf carts to drive around the community.

Location: Emerald Bay, Great ExumaThings to do nearby: Emerald Bay Beach, golf, Exuma boat excursions

Number of guests: 4Bed and bath: 2 bedrooms, 2 bathsWhy we love it: Bayfront balcony, rooftop sunset views, walkable location

There's a lovely sense of everyday island life at this two-bedroom apartment overlooking Anchor Bay. From the balcony, guests can watch boats coming and going, while the shared rooftop gallery is a particularly nice place to catch the sunset. The apartment has a well-equipped kitchen and two en suite bedrooms, and restaurants and shops are within walking distance. Beach chairs, towels, and a cooler are provided for exploring Eleuthera's coastline, making it easy to head out for the day.

Location: Governor's Harbour, EleutheraThings to do nearby: French Leave Beach, Haynes Library, Governor's Harbour restaurants

#6241. White House warns Democrats against aggressive oversight

Rep. Robert Garcia, D-Calif., is expected to lead the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call file photo)

The Trump administration signaled it would respond aggressively to a Democratic-led Congress with a letter this week threatening to prosecute lawmakers for oversight efforts.

The letter from White House Counsel Will Scharf sent Monday to House Oversight and Government Reform ranking member Robert Garcia, D-Calif., argued that members of Congress have limited authority to conduct oversight of a presidential administration and that some of the threats to issue subpoenas “may cross the line into blatant criminality.”

The letter, obtained from a White House official, marks the latest escalation from the Trump administration ahead of Democrats taking control of both chambers of Congress next year. It also dovetails with years of Trump’s threats to prosecute his critics.

“We are monitoring the abusive and capricious threats that are now proliferating from Democrat legislators who seek to abuse the legislative process to intimidate and to interfere with the lawful functioning of government,” the letter says.

Garcia, the likely committee chair next Congress, pushed back on the threat in a statement Wednesday, accusing the administration of having “something to hide” and that Congress has wide authority to investigate the executive branch.

“The American people voted overwhelmingly for us to pass laws to root out corruption and abuse," Garcia said. "The Trump Administration continues to weaponize the government with threats of unconstitutional attacks on Congress. We are a co-equal branch of government and will not be deterred by baseless threats from a weaponized DOJ or from the President’s lawyers.”

The letter came after Attorney General Todd Blanche previously refused to rule out criminal charges against members of Congress in response to investigations.

"It depends on what the crime is and what they have done,” Blanche told CNN over the weekend.

Last week, President Donald Trump himself said that threats of investigations and impeachment were “extortion at the highest level” and called for the Justice Department to “look into this criminal act, immediately!”

He also singled out Sen. Elissa Slotkin, D-Mich., calling for her to be imprisoned. The administration previously unsuccessfully attempted to indict Slotkin and other Democrats over a video she published calling for soldiers to disobey illegal orders.

And Trump last year publicly called for longtime critic Sen. Adam B. Schiff, D-Calif., to face unspecified charges in a post on Truth Social addressed to then-Attorney General Pam Bondi that also called for the prosecution of former FBI Director James Comey and New York Attorney General Letitia James. Both have faced criminal charges, pleaded not guilty and fought them in court as political attacks.

Garcia and other Democrats have signaled they intend to pursue oversight aggressively in the new Congress. After Democrats won the House majority last week, Garcia put out an all-caps statement urging administration officials to “LAWYER UP” ahead of the new year.

Garcia, as well as other likely incoming chairs such as House Judiciary ranking member Rep. Jamie Raskin, D-Md.; Homeland Security ranking member Rep. Bennie Thompson, D-Miss.; and Sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., have hinted at broad inquiries ranging from the handling of files related to deceased sex offender Jeffrey Epstein to immigration enforcement and more.

Raskin told reporters last week that he thought Democratic oversight efforts could dovetail with the party’s broader effort to address affordability issues, including by addressing the Iran war, allegations of corruption within the Trump administration and more.

“We're going to get all the information that we need in order to restore the rule of law in American constitutional democracy,” Raskin said.

The letter also echoes a previous fight the administration pitched with the House in the first Trump administration, where officials resisted in court allowing former White House Counsel Don McGahn to testify to the House Judiciary Committee for years.

#6240. Holafly Plans: The Best eSIM Plan for Long Term Travelers

There are a lot of eSIM companies in the world. They all work a similar way: you download their app, pick your package, install the eSIM into your smartphone, and off you go. There’s many I like.

But one I like more than the rest is Holafly and I’ve been using their eSIMs for years. I find their app to be easy to use and their rates really competitive.

So when Holafly launched Holafly Plans, a single eSIM that works as an ongoing subscription across 160+ destinations, I was excited. It’s a great option for those who are looking for more data and flexibility than a traditional eSIM. (An eSIM is a digital SIM built directly into your phone’s hardware, so there’s no physical card to insert or swap. Instead of visiting a shop for a plastic SIM, you activate a plan by scanning a QR code or installing it through an app, and you’re connected within minutes. Because it’s software-based, a single phone can hold multiple eSIMs, letting you switch between a home number and a local or global travel plan without touching your device. I have like 10 installed. lol)

In this post, I’m going to explain what the product is, how it’s different than a traditional eSIM, and who I think this option is for!

Holafly Plans is a single global eSIM that covers more than 160 destinations on one ongoing subscription. You buy it once, install it once, and it just keeps working as you move from country to country. You don’t reswap SIMs, you don’t redownload anything, there’s no re-purchasing, and no hunting for a new QR code every time you land somewhere new.

It automatically reconnects you when you land in a new place. Think of it as like a traditional mobile carrier – but a lot cheaper.

You can buy it monthly or annually and it comes in two tiers: Light and Unlimited. There’s no annual contract and you can cancel any time.

The Unlimited Plan includes no data caps and an unlimited hotspot so you can tether your laptop on the go. If you’re a digital nomad uploading video, doing video calls, or just someone who doesn’t want to think about data ever again, this is a great add-on. This tier also comes with a local phone number from the US, UK, or Canada, which lets you receive SMS messages.

The Light Plan gives you 25GB of data a month, still includes a hotspot, and still covers the same 160+ destination coverage. For someone who mostly uses maps, messaging apps, and the occasional Instagram scroll, this package is probably the best option.

Additionally, with both Holafly Plans, once your plan is active, you get their “Always On” feature which is 1GB of backup data every month, automatically for life, even if you eventually cancel your subscription entirely.

Pricing varies a bit by region and currency and depending on how long you purchase, so check out their current rates on the Holafly Plans page. However, as an example, their unlimited plan is only $55 USD per month for 1 year, which is a lot cheaper than any US based carrier charges for their base option that includes unlimited 5G data overseas.  You can get monthly, quarterly, or yearly plans. Quarterly plans save approximately 10% while yearly plans save 15%.

Use the promo code NOMADICMATT at checkout to get 10% OFF Holafly Plans and 5% OFF all standard Holafly eSIMs.

Classic Holafly eSIMs are built for a single trip. You pick a country or region (there are 200+ available), choose how many days of data you need, and it covers just that trip. If you’re flying to Portugal for two weeks, a classic eSIM is still the simpler, cheaper option. It’s a one-and-done purchase. If you only take a couple trips per year then this is still the best option.

On the other hand, if you’re a digital nomad who is gone from your home country most of the year and moving between different countries all the time, then the Holafly Plans fly is the much better option. It’s a standing global subscription designed for people who are more or less always somewhere. Instead of buying a new eSIM every time your itinerary changes, you have one number, one connection, one bill that follows you across borders indefinitely. Plus, you can get a phone number, unlimited data, and a hotspot. In the US, if you were to get T-Mobile’s plan, which caps data and is the closest thing we have to “affordable” international plans, you’re going to spend over $100 USD a month (I know because I used to use this plan!). #6238. Don’t Scan This Abroad: The QR Code Travel Scam Tourists Miss

QR codes are everywhere when we travel now, on restaurant tables, parking meters, hotel signs, airports, train stations, and transit machines. This travel scam known as Quishing or QR code phishing is becoming the fastest growing travel scam warning out there. Most QR codes are legitimate, but scammers are using fake QR code stickers and fake payment pages to catch travellers when they are tired, rushed, or distracted.

QR code travel scam happens when a fake QR code sends travellers to a fraudulent website. The code may be placed over a real QR code on a parking meter, restaurant table, hotel notice, airport sign, or transit machine, or it may arrive by text or email pretending to be a fine, toll, ticket, or check-in request. The safest rule is simple: Pause. Check. Then pay.Read out post: 20 Common Travel Scams and How to Avoid Them

A scammer does not always need to hack a system or damage a payment machine. Sometimes they print a fake QR code sticker and place it directly over a legitimate code.

From a quick glance, the sign still looks official. The logo may look familiar. The instructions may seem normal. The page that opens may copy the colours, layout, and branding of the real company.

You think you are paying for parking, ordering food, checking into a hotel, or settling a toll. Instead, criminals may be collecting your credit card number, password, phone number, licence plate, email address, or other personal information.

The FTC has also warned about fake traffic violation texts that begin with a QR code and try to scare people into paying a fake unpaid balance.

The FTC has warned that scammers hide harmful links in QR codes to steal personal information, including by placing fake QR codes over real ones on parking meters.

Many restaurants now use QR codes for menus, ordering, or payment. Most are legitimate, but travellers should still be cautious. This is the easiest travel scam for QR code phishing as everyone uses it.

A menu QR code should usually show a menu. Be careful if it asks for information it does not need, such as your passport number, banking details, hotel room number, or a password.

Before scanning a QR code on a restaurant table, look at the surface. Does it look printed into the menu or table sign, or does it look like a sticker placed on top? If it looks raised, crooked, bubbled, or mismatched, ask staff for a printed menu or the restaurant’s official website.

Parking is one of the easiest places for this scam to work because travellers are often rushed and confused.

You may not know the local parking app. You may be dealing with another language. You may be worried about getting a ticket. That pressure makes a “scan to pay” sticker feel helpful.

Before paying through a parking QR code, inspect the sticker, read the URL preview, and check whether the payment page matches the city, parking authority, or official app named on the machine.

If anything feels off, do not use the QR code. Type the official website yourself, use the official parking app, pay at the machine, or ask local staff for help.

Airports and transit stations are full of QR codes: Wi-Fi, directions, tickets, luggage storage, forms, lounge access, and service information. Travel scams often happen when travelers are in a hurry. If you need wifi, a taxi, some food, QR codes are often the easiest way to catch you off guard.

That does not mean every code is unsafe. It means you should slow down when a public QR code asks for payment, passwords, ID documents, or personal information.

The FBI warns that malicious QR codes can send people to fake sites, steal victim data, embed malware, or redirect payments. The FBI warns that criminals can tamper with QR codes to redirect payments, steal login and financial information, or send people to malicious websites.

The easiest way to avoid this scam is to build one habit before you scan a public QR code.

Do not scan just because a sign looks official. Public signs, parking meters, table cards, and posters can be tampered with.

If the message says you must pay immediately, avoid a fine, settle a toll, confirm a booking, or prevent a penalty, slow down. Urgency is one of the biggest warning signs.

Before your phone opens anything, look at the QR code itself.

We call this the scratch test. You are not damaging the sign. You are simply checking whether the QR code feels or looks different from the rest of the surface.

Canadian readers can also check the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security’s QR code safety guidance and report fraud through the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre.

Most phones show a preview of the website before opening the page. Read it.

Look for misspellings, extra words, strange endings, random letters, shortened links, or a domain that does not match the company, hotel, restaurant, city, or attraction.

Do not rely only on the padlock symbol. A secure connection does not automatically mean the site is legitimate. The real question is whether you are on the correct website.

The FTC has also warned about fake traffic violation texts that include a QR code and pressure people to pay a fake unpaid balance.

For payments, passwords, account logins, or identity information, the safest option is often to bypass the QR code.

Open your browser and type the official website yourself. Use an app you already installed from the official app store. Ask an employee for the correct payment method. Contact your hotel, airline, rental car company, or bank through the phone number on your booking or card — not through the number on a suspicious page.

First, do not panic. Scanning a QR code does not automatically mean your information has been stolen. The bigger risk usually begins when you enter payment information, type a password, download a file, or provide personal details.

Close the page immediately if the link looks wrong, the message creates urgency, or the site asks for information you did not expect to provide.

Do not download an unfamiliar app or file from a QR code.

If you entered credit card information, contact your bank or card issuer using the official number on the back of your card or through the official banking app.

If you entered a password, change it through the official website or app. If you reused that password anywhere else, change it there too.

Watch for follow-up messages. A scammer who has some of your information may later pretend to be your bank, hotel, airline, rental car company, or payment provider.

Report the fake QR code to the business, parking authority, hotel, airport, or local authority so they can remove it.

A QR code may be suspicious if it looks like a sticker placed over another code, has peeling edges, opens a strange URL, uses a shortened link, creates urgency, asks for information that does not make sense, or directs you away from the official website or app.

At a restaurant, a QR menu should not need your passport or banking password. At a parking meter, the payment page should match the city or parking authority. At a hotel, a check-in code should not send you to a random payment page outside the official booking system.

The BBB has also warned consumers to double-check QR codes before paying for parking.

No. QR codes are part of modern travel, and many are perfectly safe.

The goal is not to panic every time you see one. The goal is to stop treating every QR code as automatically trustworthy.

A few seconds of inspection can protect you from a much longer financial or account-recovery problem later.

QR codes are convenient, but convenience is exactly what scammers are using against travellers.

Before scanning a public QR code at a restaurant, parking meter, hotel, airport, train station, attraction, or transit stop, remember the rule:

Inspect the code. Read the link. Go directly to the official website or app when money, passwords, or personal information are involved.

That tiny pause may be the thing that saves your trip.

Scanning a QR code is not automatically dangerous. The danger usually begins when you open a suspicious page, enter payment details, type a password, download a file, or provide personal information without checking whether the site is legitimate.

Inspect the physical code for stickers, raised edges, bubbles, peeling corners, or anything placed over another code. Then check the URL preview before opening the page. If the link looks strange or does not match the official company, city, hotel, or attraction, do not use it.

Before entering payment information, make sure the website belongs to the official business or authority. When in doubt, use the official app, type the website manually, pay directly at the machine, or ask staff for the correct payment method.

Contact your bank or card issuer immediately using the official number on the back of your card or your banking app. Watch for suspicious charges, replace the card if needed, and do not use any contact information from the suspicious website.

#6237. Another bill to release Epstein files headed to House floor

Massie will force another vote on releasing files in the Jeffrey Epstein case. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call file photo)

As Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., enters his final weeks in Congress, he is one step closer to another vote on legislation related to the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

A discharge petition led by Massie aimed at extracting more files from the Justice Department has now received enough support to force a vote on the House floor.

Rep. John Garamendi, D-Calif., was the decisive 218th signature on the discharge petition, a procedural tool allowing rank-and-file House members to register their support for a piece of legislation and circumvent leadership to force a vote. Massie and other supporters of the effort say the bill is a bid for transparency.

Earlier this week, Massie said his pitch to his colleagues was simple.

“They could be a hero if they sign it,” he said, as he chased down the final two signatures as the House returned from recess on Monday. Rep. Adam Smith, D-Wash., signed just before Garamendi.

Massie’s time left in office is ticking down after a challenger backed by President Donald Trump ousted him in his GOP primary earlier this year.

The petition marks the second push led by Massie to require the release of the Epstein files. Last fall, Massie and Rep. Ro Khanna, D-Calif., led a discharge petition on a bill dubbed the Epstein Files Transparency Act, which directed the Justice Department to publicly release documents in its possession related to Epstein and his associate Ghislaine Maxwell.

The bill passed the House by a vote of 427-1 last November, and in the Senate a few days later. Trump signed the measure shortly afterward.

In a statement this summer, Massie said he believes the Justice Department is still withholding more than 3 million files that it is required to release under the November 2025 law and is “maintaining heavy redactions” on others.

The new bill would allow state attorneys general, local prosecutors and victims to sue the federal government for withholding such documents. It would also allow victims to privately view unredacted versions of any records that mention them.

Now that the new petition has reached 218 signatures, it must sit for seven legislative days before being called up by anyone who signed it. Last time around, Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., scheduled a House vote on the initial Epstein bill before that ripening period was over, saying it was a foregone conclusion that the legislation would reach the floor.

Other Republicans who have signed on to the petition this year include Reps. Nancy Mace, R-S.C.; Ralph Norman, R-S.C., and Brian Fitzpatrick, R-Pa., none of whom will be returning next Congress. Rep. Lauren Boebert, R-Colo., backed the initial effort last fall, but her name did not appear on the petition this time.

Allies of the issue in Congress have faced pushback from Trump. While the president suggested during his 2024 reelection campaign that he was open to declassifying some Epstein documents, Trump then shifted gears, calling them a “hoax.”

“Once you get to 218, you can never sign it," Massie said. "There's nobody left, no spots left. It goes straight to the floor, and then you can vote for it. But you were never part of the group that actually got it to the floor."

Away proves that great design and thoughtful functionality don’t have to come at a steep price. The brand’s lineup of best-selling luggage under $300 includes sleek staples like The Carry-On ($275) and The Bigger Carry-On ($295)—lightweight, durable pieces that glide effortlessly through terminals and tuck neatly into overhead bins. You can explore more travel-ready finds in Away’s Under $300 collection.

For families, Away’s Family Travel collection makes group trips easier with space-maximizing suitcases, kids’ luggage, diaper bags, crossbody bags, and even pet carriers. Larger pieces like The Medium Flex and The Trunk offer extra capacity and deep compartments, perfect for storing everyone’s essentials in one place.

A great way to save on luggage that's new to you and help reduce waste? Away Reclaimed, the brand's hub for secondhand luggage. Many pieces go for up to $100 less than their original retail value, and each item is graded on a scale of ‘Good’ to ‘Great’ to ‘Excellent’, based on how many cosmetic flaws are present. Per Away, every item is in “travel-ready condition,” and the “surfaces and interiors are cleaned and refreshed.” As you can imagine, inventory comes and goes fairly quickly. If you have something specific in mind, know that you can select the “Notify Me” button on any item page to receive an email notification when the size and color you're looking for becomes available.

Away’s appeal goes beyond its minimalist design—it’s the thoughtful details that make the brand a trusted travel companion. Orders over $100 ship free, and if something isn’t quite right, you can return or exchange unused items within 100 days, either online or at one of Away’s 17 stores. Every suitcase is backed by a lifetime warranty, covering functional repairs so your luggage lasts trip after trip.

There’s purpose behind the polish, too: With sustainability in mind, Away incorporates more recycled materials into its luggage and ships everything in 100% recyclable packaging. And with Shop Pay, you can choose interest-free installments to make investing in quality gear a little easier.

If your Away promo code isn't working at checkout, don't panic—there are a few simple things you can do. First, double check that the code is spelled correctly with no extra spaces or typos. If that doesn't work, take a look at the exact details of the promo code to make sure it's still active and hasn't expired already. Keep in mind that some discount codes have a minimum spend requirement, so you'll want to be sure you've hit any necessary criteria for the deal. If everything looks right and your Away promo code still isn't working, clear your browser's cache and give the page a refresh. Shoppers can also contact Away's customer service for help.

#6235. Rand Paul chooses ranking member slot at Senate HELP

Sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky., leaves the Senate Republicans’ lunch in the Capitol on Tuesday. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call) (Bill Clark CQ Roll Call)

Sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky., announced Wednesday he plans to serve as the top Republican on the Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee when Democrats take control of Congress next year.

The move clears the way for Senate Ethics Chairman James Lankford, R-Okla., to use his seniority to ascend to ranking Republican on the Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee, which Paul currently chairs, and touches off several other shifts at the top of other committees.

The move fit in with Sen. Lisa Murkowski’s bid to use her seniority to succeed Senate Appropriations Chair Susan Collins, R-Maine, as top Republican on the Appropriations panel. If Paul did not go to the top spot on HELP, Murkowski, R-Alaska, would be next in line for that committee in the next Congress.

Murkowski is second in seniority on Appropriations to Collins, who was defeated for reelection. But she faces a potential challenge from Sen. Jerry Moran, R-Kan., who is next in line behind her.

Paul said in a press release that he plans to bring the same approach to the HELP Committee as he did as chairman of Homeland, where he said he “challenged entrenched bureaucracies, forced federal officials to answer for their actions, and pulled back the curtain on what Washington tried to keep hidden.”

He cited calling Dr. Anthony Fauci before the committee to probe the former federal health official’s role in pandemic-related shutdowns and the origin of the COVID-19 virus, and releasing thousands of pages of pandemic-related documents. The panel voted in August to hold Fauci in criminal contempt of Congress for declining to answer questions about the pandemic during a highly charged hearing.

Related: Fauci could face criminal contempt charge following panel vote

Paul, an ophthalmologist, said at HELP he will “stand against efforts to put Washington between Americans and their doctors, their children’s schools, and their paychecks.” He predicted “a rush toward socialism unlike anything we have seen” when the Democrat-controlled Congress convenes in January.

Lankford, in a separate statement, confirmed his interest in becoming the ranking member of the Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee. In many areas, he said, the panel can work in a bipartisan manner, and over the past decade he “worked across the aisle to improve emergency communications in federal buildings, strengthen the United States Postal Service, increase federal cybersecurity preparedness, government transparency, and the use of artificial intelligence.”

But he added that his job also would be to “push back on a [Democratic] majority that goes too far . . . Oversight is responsible, but obstruction is unacceptable.”

Lankford said he would work together with the likely committee chair, Sen. Maggie Hassan, D-N.H., “when we can agree and be a fierce opposition if there is an attempt to undercut our nation’s security.”

#6234. The 40 Best Resorts in the Caribbean: 2026 Readers’ Choice Awards

Trends come and go, but here at Condé Nast Traveler, one thing never changes: your insatiable appetite for seeing the world. This year, our readers cast an almighty 798,867 votes in our 39th Readers’ Choice Awards to tell us about the planet’s best travel experiences: You fell hard for palace hotels in Morocco, cruised down the Amazon, and got swept up in New York City’s exhilarating energy. Now, read on to find out where your favorites fall among the winners—and get inspired for where to go next, whether it's to a top-rated hotel or resort, or centered around a worthy cruise, spa, or island. These are the best resorts in the world as voted by you, our readers.

View this gallery as a list of the top resorts in the Caribbean with scores here.

The namesake hillside resort set above Toiny Bay gives “wild” an unexpected new meaning when it comes to sceney St. Barts. On the shrubby southeastern point of the island, this unfussy haven is where an in-the-know social set head to find serenity. The star amenity here is the private beach, accessible via a three-minute Defender ride down switchbacking roads. Le Toiny’s stretch of soft sand is considered the sole private hotel beach on all of St. Barts. Plus, some of the oldest traditional English-style cottages on the island, dating back to the 1700s, can be found beside the beach club (one is currently used as treatment areas for the spa). The suites and villas were redesigned in 2024 to create airy living spaces that draw your eye outward to the leafy open-air surroundings and azure water views just beyond your private pool deck.

Grand Cayman may be famous for its SCUBA diving and offshore banking, but with several daily non-stops from New York and Boston, it’s increasingly drawing families to its powdery, placid western Caribbean beaches. On the island’s Seven Mile Beach—one of the loveliest stretches of sand in the world—you'll find the 266-room Kimpton Seafire Resort & Spa, with a boutique atmosphere that manages to be both child-friendly (two pools, a kids club) and hip (colorful, contemporary design, and a lobby scene replete with pool table, library, and daily happy hour). The food is also strong: Hit beachside Coccoloba for fish tacos and ceviches; Ave, the resort's primary restaurant, for epic breakfast buffets (including house-made cronuts); and the sceney Avecita for progressive Spanish fare like white anchovy toast and prawn tartare, served up alongside craft cocktails at the chef’s counter. You can always snorkel and parasail right off the hotel’s beach, but you’re also just a short ride from Stingray City (where you can stand on a sandbar and touch giant rays as they swim by), world-class gardens (look for the endangered blue iguana), golf, and roadside jerk chicken. Hit Rum Point to toast the sunset—or maybe you'll prefer doing that from your own private balcony.

This romantic all-suite beachfront retreat north of the sprawling all-inclusives of Punta Cana is a diamond literally in the rough—the last two miles of the approach road are so bone rattling that it may be worth ponying up more than $250 for the ten-minute helicopter transfer from the airport in Punta Cana. But behind the resort’s unmarked security gate, Zoëtry is breathtaking. The open-air lobby has a soaring peaked thatch roof, and the 51rooms, divided between two-story thatched buildings and freestanding villas, are arranged around two snaking pools and are no more than a one-minute walk from the beach. With classic clean lines, they are dramatic by virtue of their size (the smallest is 775 square feet) and simple comforts—wicker ceilings, dark hardwood floors and furniture, white-on-white beds, immense bathrooms with black slate showers and deep soaking tubs. The resort’s restaurants draw culinary inspiration from traditional Dominican fare and international flavors, with an emphasis on using locally grown and organic ingredients.

For toes-in-the-sand luxury with impeccable service, foodie-approved eateries, Caribbean-cool rooms, and views that will have all your friends and family seeing green, La Samanna can’t be beat. Set along the white sands of Baie Longue, known for being one of the most beautiful beaches in all of St. Martin, guests are never far from the startlingly turquoise waters, and La Samanna offers plenty of ways to get out on the water, including complimentary kayaks, paddleboards, snorkeling gear, and more. With three main restaurants—one of which changes in concept between lunch and dinner—plus a fabulous daily breakfast and top-notch room service, there’s really no reason to leave for meals. The star of the show is L’Oursin, the upscale French restaurant just off the lobby, where each table comes with a view of the sailboat-spotted sea. If you can, splurge on one of the property's eight independent villas—the double-level mansions have everything a group could need to vacation more than comfortably.

The "secret" part of Secret Bay's name is no accident—the resort's 10 gorgeous villas give new meaning to the word hideaway. Touches vary from villa to villa, but all have interiors and floors made of Guyanese Greenheart, bedroom furniture made of Dominican red cedar, open decks, private pools, and 180-degree views over the mountain peaks of Dominica and the Caribbean Sea. Though we doubt you'll get tired of living your own castaway fantasies (albeit with much nicer accommodations), Secret Bay's concierge is available to help craft personalized itineraries: think rainforest hikes with a famed naturalist, or a sunset sail along the island's western coast.

Anguilla is a small-but-mighty island packed with a handful of luxury properties, dining options, and a whole bunch of outstanding beaches. Barnes Bay and Meads Bay surround the property on both sides, with waters that are occasionally rough but known to be swimmable at other times of the year. Regardless of the conditions, white beach chairs line the sand in pristine formation each morning, and three large pool areas—two kid-friendly, and one adults-only—provide plenty of swimming options when the ocean is unavailable. The property stretches across the shore, which means each room provides a unique view of some combination of the wide property’s beachfront, ocean, palm trees, or garden areas. In the ocean-view one-bedroom suite, we overlooked the modernist pool deck as well as the distant ocean, with a plunge pool on the balcony and ample outdoor space for afternoon lounging. The bathroom was equipped with two sinks, a large tub, and a marble walk-in shower.

All rooms at this Sandals Resort are in stone buildings on a two-mile-long beach in a 500-acre wilderness preserve on the island's south coast. The resort is arranged as three European villages—Dutch, French, and Italian (including a Venetian piazza)—and the architecture includes lots of marble columns and vaulted ceilings. "Buildings are spread out, but it still feels like an intimate retreat." Rooms differ according to village: French rooms have mahogany four-poster beds and Caribbean decor, while Italian rooms are heavy on marble. The plantation-style Eleanor's, complete with a waterwheel and a stone fireplace, serves contemporary Caribbean cuisine.

Though the Buccaneer, on the U.S. Virgin Island of St. Croix, has been proudly run by the Armstrong family for over 70 years—it's the longest-running resort in the Caribbean—its history dates even further back to the property's earliest construction by a Knight of Malta in 1653. Since then, it's been a private home; a sugar mill; a cotton estate, then a cattle estate; and now, an incredibly warm, family-friendly resort that's more like a country club. You have access to an 18-hole golf course, eight tennis courts, three beaches (whether you prefer kayaking and snorkeling or lounging in peace and quiet), a full water sports center, and none of the pretense. Arrive for lunch at the Grotto in your bathing suit, and please don't sleep through the terrific breakfast buffet. The Buccanneer knows how to put out a spread. Once you're done moving about for the day, settle into the deluxe oceanfront room—the resort's most popular—and lie on your bed beneath the 16-foot-high wood ceilings, watching the waves lap the beach out your picture window.

The tiny volcanic island of Grenada is both an unexpected and obvious choice for Six Senses’ foray into the Caribbean. Compared to big-hitting neighbors like St. Lucia and Antigua, it has been overlooked by travelers to the region. But this means that it remains largely uncrowded and retains a more rustic version of tourism. Six Senses has done well to anchor itself to that. Here, your welcome ritual begins with a sensory spice “tour;” its 56 suites and 15 villas are stylish but designed to sit unobtrusively on the landscape; and its curated excursions—from rainforest hikes to Rastafarian farm visits—spotlight the best of Grenada’s natural bounty. In classic Six Senses style, wellness is a key protagonist, and you can seek out everything from aerial yoga to sleep therapy, as well as treatments like the Caribbean Cleansing Ritual that nod to the surroundings. It’s very tempting to stay put, heading to the spa or sipping rum cocktails poolside, but you’d do well to pair off with one of the property’s community hosts and head out: to spice-laden markets in its photogenic capital or for a bit of beachside limin’ (defined locally as “kicking with friends”), a beloved national pastime.

The old adage of getting what you pay for rings true here, and while it may be a splurge, it will be an unforgettable stay. The rooms are quiet, the beds are comfortable, and in my opinion, this is the best stretch of beach on the island. If you’re looking for luxury—and budget isn’t an issue—the Ritz is the top of the line. Guests who stay in the 320 spacious and chic rooms can expect to be spoiled. Servers cruise around the shore on Segway scooters, effortlessly balancing trays of tropical cocktails. The concierge can secure reservations for you at sold-out restaurants, set up offsite tours, and suggest itineraries for any kind of traveler. The 15,000-square-foot spa at the Ritz is one of the largest and best on the island, and the property's on-site restaurants are simply divine. The vibe is upscale without being stuffy, with guests in the elevators side by side wearing pool towels and Prada.

A relatively new addition to St. Barts' luxury hotel scene, Le Barthélemy is a sophisticated winner that keeps with the island's low-rise sensibility. Set between a lagoon and Grand Cul-de-Sac beach along the island's northeastern shore, the hotel is an education in understated elegance. Rooms are spare and enormous, with lots of wood and one or two pops of bright color—some even have small, rectangular plunge pools for mini-laps. The food at  Amis St. Barth is unabashedly modern French, with attention paid to proper portions in the tropics: in other words, not too much. Water sports enthusiasts have an expanse of calm shallow waters for kayaking, kite-surfing, and snorkeling—a flotilla of a dozen sea turtles that survived the storms of 2017 remain in residence and are easily visible.

Those who knew and loved Le Carl Gustaf the first time around will have even more reason to fall for it now that the Barriere group has taken over. The hotelier company—known for reviving particularly beloved but withering properties—has made sure to keep the spirit of Le Carl chic and easy. The raw wood and petite terraces still make it feel like the beach house of a fabulous French friend, yet the hotel’s reimagined approach to the environment gives it a 21st-century edge. Paris design firm Gilles and Boissier gussied up the 21 rooms with creams, stone, and linen, as well as a profusion of palms separating various spaces with a curtain of greenery. Suites have been reconfigured to catch sea breezes, providing natural air conditioning. And a fleet of electric bikes brings guests down the hill upon which the hotel stands like a lookout, over the town and coastline, to nearby Shell Beach, the perfect place for a picnic prepared by the hotel’s staff that feels, appropriately simple and chic—much like Le Carl itself.

Romance is taken to a whole other level at this adults-only St. Lucia resort. With 36 plunge pool suites, butler service, and a personalized bar with only the top-shelf, this enclave was made for couples to relax and reconnect. While there's no shortage of places to lounge or splash around in on property, the resort also offers an array of excursions to explore the gorgeous corner of the Caribbean St. Lucia lays claim to. From rainforest nature walks with a fully packed picnic basket to adrenaline-pumping ATV tours, Serenity at Coconut Bay knows there's many ways to take in all the gorgeous scenery.

#6233. Scott Colom elected Mississippi’s first Black senator since Reconstruction

Mississippi Democrat Scott Colom, here at a news conference in Jackson on Nov. 4, has defeated Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith. (Rogelio V. Solis/Getty Images)

Democrat Scott Colom has unseated Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith to become Mississippi’s first Black senator since Reconstruction.

The result is a stunning flip for Democrats in a deep-red state where they last won a Senate election in 1982, and it brings the Senate Democratic Caucus to at least 55 seats in the next Congress.

Colom was leading Hyde-Smith 49.2 percent to 48.7 percent — or by just over 4,600 votes out of more than 960,000 cast — when The Associated Press called the race Wednesday, a little over a week after Election Day. Ty Pinkins, the 2024 Democratic Senate nominee who ran as an independent this year, had 2 percent.

In recent days, as absentee and provisional ballots were counted, Colom had all but declared victory, repeatedly saying that Hyde-Smith had no path to victory.

“I'll work every day in the U.S. Senate to build a future that generations of Mississippians can be just as proud to call home,” he posted Monday on social media.

With his victory, Colom joins several other Democrats who flipped seats in deep-red states, including Texas’ James Talarico, Kansas’ Adam Hamilton and South Carolina’s Annie Andrews. Democrats have so far flipped eight Senate seats to win control of the chamber, overcoming a difficult Senate map and giving them their largest majority in the chamber since 2011.

That majority could expand further if Democrats flip the Senate seat in Alaska, where former Rep. Mary Peltola narrowly leads Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan.

Republicans have dominated Senate elections in Mississippi in recent decades. The last Democrat to be elected senator in the Magnolia State was John C. Stennis, who won his sixth full and final term in 1982. Colom will be the third Black man to serve as a Mississippi senator after Republicans Hiram Revels and Blanche Bruce during Reconstruction.

While Revels and Bruce, who left office in 1881, were elected by the state Legislature, Colom will be the first Black senator elected directly by voters.

Colom has served as a district attorney for four counties in northeast Mississippi since 2016. President Joe Biden nominated him for a federal district judgeship in 2022, but Hyde-Smith effectively blocked his nomination by not returning a so-called blue slip, a Senate Judiciary Committee tradition that lets senators derail district judge nominees in their home states.

Senate Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer said last week that he’d had Colom in his sights for several years as a potential Senate candidate, including for a race against the state’s senior senator, Republican Roger Wicker.

“I had Scott Colom and his father come to my house, and I served them a nice little brunch or something. I said, ‘You got to run,’” the New York Democrat recalled to MS NOW. “They were smarter than me. This was four years ago. They said, ‘We don’t want to run this time, but we know that Hyde-[Smith], the incumbent, is so weak, we could beat her.’”

Still, the Mississippi race didn’t capture as much national attention as other Senate contests until the closing weeks of the campaign. A trio of Black senators, Angela Alsobrooks of Maryland, Lisa Blunt Rochester of Delaware and Cory Booker of New Jersey, all campaigned with Colom throughout the summer and fall. Key national figures, including former President Bill Clinton, former Vice President Kamala Harris and former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg, also stumped for him in October.

Colom’s campaign engaged voters with quirky ads and unconventional forms of outreach, including meeting with people lining up to attend a Trump rally. One ad that went viral played on Hyde Smith saying earlier this year that people had “so many proteins to choose from” when asked about rising beef prices.

“Pick another protein?” says a man in the ad. “I’d rather pick another senator instead.”

Major Democratic outside groups made a late play in the state, with WinSenate, which is affiliated with Senate Democrats’ top super PAC, investing $2.2 million. The Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee spent $500,000 on a coordinated ad buy late last month.

The pro-Republican Senate Leadership Fund dropped $1.7 million on the race, and Trump headlined a rally for Hyde-Smith on Oct. 26.

#6232. My Favorite Villa: A Storybook Trullo in Puglia With Six Bedrooms, a Private Chef, and Olive Grove Views

My best friend and I had an entire six-bedroom estate in Puglia, Italy, to ourselves for three nights in early November. We could have invited another 10 people, but there was something rather wonderful about having all that space for just the two of us. The region's whitewashed streets had emptied of their summer crowds, and the countryside around our home away from home was quiet enough that we felt no particular urgency to go anywhere.

I'd been looking forward to sleeping in a trullo, one of the traditional dry-stone houses with conical roofs that dot this part of southern Italy. At Trullo delle Dame, my bedroom sat directly beneath one of those cones, and every night, I fell asleep looking up at the curved stone ceiling. It felt like a storybook hideaway reimagined by someone with a very good eye for design. The soaking tub in my room didn't hurt either.

The original stone walls and domed ceilings have been preserved throughout the restored trulli, with sleek off-white furniture, stone walls, and traditional glazed ceramic or terra-cotta ornaments called pumi strewn about. The six bedrooms, including five en suite bedrooms and a primary suite, are spread out across the property. While I was there with my friend, I kept thinking about how well the house would work for a multigenerational family trip. There's enough space for everyone to retreat to their own rooms, and plenty of reasons to come back together over a chef-prepared meal, a card game in the seating area overlooking the countryside, or a dip in the saltwater infinity pool.

My favorite spot in the estate was the outdoor kitchen—specifically at the enormous round dining table, complete with a giant lazy Susan. One afternoon, we made orecchiette there, shaping the little ears of pasta by hand, flour up to our wrists, before sitting down to eat what we'd made. I could picture a dozen people around that table on a summer evening, passing plates of pasta and pouring each other another glass of wine (which the Mandarin Oriental team will stock the fridge with upon request).

Throughout the stay, our days fell into an easy routine. We'd walk through the olive groves in the mornings, read on the couch in the afternoons, and spend a few hours on the loungers by the pool. The water was unheated, so we were content to stay poolside in November. But I imagine it's where everyone ends up in July.

As tempting as it was to stay put, there was too much good food and wine in the surrounding countryside to spend all three days at the house. We drove the three miles into Cisternino for a meal at Taverna della Torre, and I'm still thinking about the gnocchi with white truffles. Another afternoon took us to Giovanni Aiello, an independent winery near Putignano, where we got to help make some of the bottle labels. The cellar is beautiful, and you can even have your tasting inside an old wine barrel. With the towns of Martina Franca and Ostuni also within easy driving distance, we could have happily spent a few more days eating our way around Puglia.

Some little bites, courtesy of the private chef

Of course, we hardly needed to leave the house to eat well. Each morning, our private chef laid out a breakfast spread of fresh yogurt, meats and cheeses, pies, pancakes, juices, and fruit, along with freshly brewed cappuccinos. There was enough food to feed considerably more than two people, though we did our best. In the evenings, he prepared multicourse dinners using local, seasonal produce. Of everything he made, my favorite was a fava bean purée with roasted peppers.

As two busy working moms, we quickly got used to the luxury of not having to think about what anyone would eat. Waking up to a breakfast feast and a creamy coffee, knowing someone else would deal with the dishes, was perhaps the hardest thing to give up at the end of the trip. (My family may need to lower their breakfast expectations for the foreseeable future.) And while we thoroughly enjoyed our few days off from mom duties, I could see how having a chef would make a family vacation feel much more like a vacation for the parents too. No grocery runs, no figuring out what to cook for 12 people, and no kitchen to clean up afterward.

The writer participating in a pasta-making class in the outdoor kitchen

The fruits of their labor: lots of orecchiette!

If we came back with our kids, I'd happily sign them up for a pizza-making session while we snuck off for a massage in the olive groves, all activities the brand offers to guests. The trees, which produce the estate's own olive oil, also make a rather lovely setting for a yoga class, which can also be arranged during the warmer months.

A few things worth knowing before booking: The private chef, food, and drinks are charged separately from the villa rental. You'll also want a car to explore the neighboring towns, although the concierge can arrange transfers. And if you're coming in November, as we did, check restaurant opening hours before heading out, since some places shorten their hours after the summer season. The unheated pool is also worth keeping in mind if you're traveling with children outside the warmer months.

On the morning we left, our chef packed us meat-and-cheese sandwiches for the road. After three days of elaborate breakfasts and multicourse dinners, those sandwiches somehow ranked among my favorite things he'd made. As we drove away, I thought about how I'd happily come back with a houseful of friends and family in summer—but I'd want the same bedroom under the cone.

#6231. Some Democrats doubt Trump is serious about cutting deals in new Congress

President Donald Trump speaks with reporters on the South Lawn of the White House on Oct. 13 before leaving for a campaign rally in Alaska. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call)

President Donald Trump’s postelection statements about working with Democrats have presented the incoming majority with a kaleidoscope to decipher, but some Democratic lawmakers have their doubts.

On the one hand, the Republican president has contended that he can work with House and Senate Democrats after the new Congress is seated in January, even floating a bipartisan immigration bill. But on the other, he promoted his hard-line aide Stephen Miller to White House chief of staff, raising doubts about any cooling of the political environment.

At every stop along his October campaign rally blitz before Republicans suffered massive losses on Nov. 3, Trump railed against “Dumbocrats” and their “bad” policies. He mocked their candidates as too extreme, too corrupt and too beholden to the most progressive wing of their party. He even warned that, if voters handed them control of the House and Senate, it would set off “a 1929-style economic depression.”

Voters ignored him. They handed House Democrats over 250 seats at least come January, and the party will have at least 54 seats in the Senate.

Trump was asked during a “60 Minutes” interview taped Friday afternoon at the White House if he could resist insulting Democratic lawmakers for six months if that’s how long it took to reach a deal on major legislation. “Very easily,” he responded.

But several Democrats are so sure about getting to a “Kumbaya” moment with Trump during his final two years.

Virginia Sen. Tim Kaine said it was hard to take the president at his word because he is “so unpredictable.”

“But I'm certainly telling my colleagues we should try to put as many bills as we can on his desk that do good things for the American public, and then see how he behaves,” he said Tuesday.

"We're gonna put bills in front of the president on affordability starting Day One,” California Rep. Robert Garcia, the likely incoming House Oversight and Government Reform chair, said Tuesday. “We'll have to see if he's serious, but I don't trust Donald Trump for a second.”

The White House on Monday sent Garcia a letter, obtained by CQ Roll Call, warning House Democrats that their anticipated spate of probes "may cross the line into blatant criminality."

Rep. Jim McGovern, a Massachusetts Democrat who is in line to chair the Rules Committee in the new Congress, said on the floor Tuesday that he does not see a GOP that is ready to heed the election's lessons and come to the bargaining table.

“Instead of taking the hint or listening to the overwhelming majority of Americans who told them to change course, Republicans are doubling down on the same tactics and messaging they've been jamming down our throats these last two years, and it's a perfect example of why they lost in the first place,” he said. “They do not listen.

“Then to double down even further, the failed lame-duck president appointed Stephen Miller, the architect of all the cruel policies that most people hate, as his new White House chief of staff,” McGovern added, referring to the Trump administration’s immigration crackdown. “What planet are these people living on?”

Kaine said congressional Democrats might not notice that much of a change from the White House with Miller moving into the chief’s suite near the Oval Office.

“Stephen Miller was calling a lot of the shots, even if he wasn't chief of staff,” the Virginia Democrat said. “So I view that as a kind of a change of the face, but not of the character of the administration.”

House Republicans’ Tuesday vote to make hard-line conservative Jim Jordan of Ohio their next leader is another red flag for Democrats.

“White House Chief of staff Stephen Miller and House Minority Leader Jim Jordan,” Brendan Duke, a former senior Democratic Senate aide now with the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities, wrote on X. “Where is the pivot to the center after a historic election loss?”

Getting to the center is what retiring Nebraska Rep. Don Bacon says his fellow Republicans and Trump should be doing after the election massacre.

"I do wish we could get to the point where we could solve big problems, instead of just beating the other side,” said Bacon, who has floated a 2028 presidential bid. “We can’t do this Republican-only or Democrat-only. And I would say this to the president, too: We’ve got to start working across the aisle to solve these problems.”

Despite his postelection talk of working with Democrats, Trump has sought to blame them for an up-and-down U.S. stock market.

“Right after the election it went down $3 trillion,” he said Monday during an unplanned White House press briefing. “That was because of the result of the election, because the stock market does not want to see Democrats. And your 401(k)s have gone way down because of the ridiculous result.”

He's also returned this week to questioning the midterm results: “It's not even a result. It's almost hard to believe. Now, I wasn't on the ballot.”

Members of House Republicans’ new leadership team on Tuesday sounded dug in and ready for a partisan brawl over Democrats’ promised investigations into the president, many of his top aides and Trump family members. Jordan's election as GOP leader shows that “we are ready to dig in for the fight,” outgoing Speaker Mike Johnson told reporters Tuesday.

Michigan Rep. Lisa McClain, who was reelected House GOP conference chair, pointed to Garcia's two-word statement on Election Day: "Lawyer up."

“Tell me how ‘lawyering up’ helps anybody with affordability?" she said. “They're going to be focused on going after President Trump. We are going to be focused on improving the quality of life for every American.”

To that end, retiring Maryland Rep. Steny H. Hoyer, a former No. 2 House Democrat, said Republicans should heed one big takeaway from the election: “Trump lost.”
